title: Conflict is producing a compound health-systems crisis through displacement, infrastructure damage, access restrictions, supply gaps, and interrupted continuity of care
source_unit: World Health Organization, Middle East Escalation of Conflict, Global external situation report No. 11, data as of 14 September 2026
geography: Conflict-affected countries in the WHO Eastern Mediterranean and European regions, including Iran, Lebanon, Iraq, Israel, Yemen, and related regional spillover risks

observations.period: Data as of 14 September 2026; selected affected countries

denominator.unit: countries with selected displacement, injury, death, or health-system indicators in the report table

reported_displacement.value: 333 in Lebanon and 77,798 in Yemen in the report’s selected country table; Iran and Iraq marked N/A

reported_injuries.value: 33,806 in Iran; 12,406 in Lebanon; 2,379 in Yemen; 300 in Iraq; 9,067 in Israel

reported_deaths.value: 3,375 in Iran; 4,383 in Lebanon; 504 in Yemen; 109 in Iraq; 26 in Israel

observations.method: WHO situation-report compilation using country reporting and operational updates; data cutoff is 14 September 2026 and country estimates may differ from other sources or be revised.
observations.uncertainty: The report explicitly notes differing data cutoffs, incomplete reporting, delayed verification, and possible upward or downward revision; figures are not a harmonized conflict mortality or displacement census.
observations.subgroup: Civilians, displaced households, injured people, patients with chronic or acute conditions, health workers, and communities in conflict-affected or return areas.
observations.counterinterpretation: Reported totals document exposure but do not alone establish service access, household coping, mortality attribution, or the relative contribution of conflict, infrastructure, disease, or underfunding.

observations.period: Data as of 14 September 2026; attacks and infrastructure impacts on health care

denominator.unit: countries with reported WHO-verified attacks on health care in the table

verified_attacks.value: 27 in Iran, 215 in Lebanon, 9 in Israel, and 1 in Yemen

lebanon_closed_facilities.value: 21 primary health-care centers and 3 hospitals remain closed in conflict-affected areas

lebanon_damaged_hospitals.value: 17 hospitals damaged, including the three that remain closed

observations.method: WHO Surveillance System for Attacks on Health Care and country operational reporting, with verification and consolidation caveats retained.
observations.uncertainty: WHO notes delays in verification and changes as data are consolidated; facility closure and damage status can change with access, repair, security, and reporting.
observations.subgroup: Patients, health workers, primary-care users, hospitals, clinics, referral networks, and communities relying on local facilities in conflict and return areas.
observations.counterinterpretation: Facility closure does not mean all care stops, since referral, outreach, temporary structures, repairs, and adjusted staffing can preserve some services while increasing travel, waiting, and access burdens.

observations.period: Data as of 14 September 2026; system and household continuity pressures

infrastructure_disruptions.value: power and water damage disrupted hospital continuity, vaccine and medicine cold chains, safe drinking water, and sanitation-related readiness in affected areas of Iran

medicine_pressure.value: shortages and significant price increases were reported for some imported or branded medicines, with particular implications for cancer, chronic-disease, and other NCD patients

yemen_reproductive_need.value: approximately 240 pregnant women were reported to need immediate access to lifesaving reproductive-health services

observations.method: WHO country situation and operational reporting linking conflict, infrastructure damage, supply chains, access, displacement, disease, and continuity of care.
observations.uncertainty: The report provides operational snapshots rather than a full population denominator, causal decomposition, or repeated household-level measurement of cost, delay, substitution, and treatment outcome.
observations.subgroup: Patients needing chronic, cancer, maternal, reproductive, mental-health, trauma, or infectious-disease services; displaced families; pregnant women; and households facing medicine-price increases.
observations.counterinterpretation: Emergency deliveries, generators, alternate facilities, and outreach can mitigate disruption, but mitigation may be temporary, geographically uneven, or unable to replace routine and specialized care.

observations.period: Data as of 14 September 2026; response capacity and funding

appeal.unit: WHO emergency appeal for health operations across five countries

funding_received.unit: reported funding received against the appeal

response_routes.value: logistics, air charters, trauma and intensive-care supplies, NCD and mental-health supplies, generators, preparedness, and emergency repairs

observations.method: WHO operational update and emergency-appeal reporting within the situation report.
observations.uncertainty: Funding received is a snapshot at the report date and does not measure disbursement timing, procurement completion, delivery, utilization, or outcome.
observations.subgroup: WHO country offices, ministries of health, health facilities, humanitarian partners, donors, and populations dependent on externally supported essential services.
observations.counterinterpretation: An underfunded appeal indicates resource constraint but does not by itself show that every planned intervention is unavailable or that funding is the only operational bottleneck.

related_sources.claim: WHO’s Middle East conflict emergency page provides the broader situation and response context.
WHO Surveillance System for Attacks on Health Care provides the attack-verification context cited in the report.

boundary: This record adds a realized conflict-health systems signal linking casualties, displacement, attacks on health care, damaged power and water infrastructure, supply chains, medicine affordability, service continuity, emergency response, and funding. It is a dated WHO situation report with country-reported estimates, not a harmonized conflict census, causal attribution, beneficiary-level panel, complete service-availability map, or outcome evaluation.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official WHO publication page and three-page PDF were reviewed for the 14 September data cutoff, country estimates, attacks on health care, facility closures and damage, infrastructure and medicine pressures, reproductive-health need, response routes, and appeal funding; reported estimates and operational claims were kept distinct from causal conclusions.
